name: Weapons That Rewrote the Rules of War
description: Spears to stealth aircraft: the inventions that turned the tide of battles, made armies obsolete and changed what it means to win.

checkpoints.name: Stone, bronze and string
checkpoints.note: Hunters made spears, throwers and bows long before cities. When metal arrived, the sword, the strong composite bow and the chariot helped build the first armies and empires.

checkpoints.name: Iron, siege and fire
checkpoints.note: Pikes, crossbows and trebuchets decided sieges and battles from Macedon to China. The Byzantines sprayed Greek fire on ships, and in China the first gunpowder weapons appeared.

checkpoints.name: Powder meets plate
checkpoints.note: Cannon broke castle walls, longbows and crossbows tested knights in armour, and muskets with bayonets turned peasants into soldiers who could beat them. Armour gradually disappeared.

checkpoints.name: Industrial killing
checkpoints.note: Factories gave armies revolvers, rapid-fire guns, machine guns and torpedoes, and navies built ironclads such as the Monitor and then the Dreadnought. Weapons could now be made in huge numbers, and soldiers faced fire that no courage could cross.

checkpoints.name: The world wars
checkpoints.note: Poison gas, tanks and submarines marked the First World War. In the Second, rockets, flamethrowers and napalm were used, and in 1945 a B-29 bomber carried the first nuclear weapon used on a city.

checkpoints.name: The nuclear age and after
checkpoints.note: Hydrogen bombs and long-range missiles made the Cold War a standoff. Rifles such as the AK-47 armed fighters everywhere, and stealth aircraft and drones brought war into the age of remote control.
